comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Semantics decided during design of epic 0e68-41eb-5782-4336 (many-to-many tracker projects), which now depends_on this bug.

CHOSEN: option 1 of this ticket's AC — skip assignee sync for tracker-unresolvable assignees. Rejected: mapping agent identities to a service account (loses the identity and still writes a wrong value to the tracker) and an unresolvable-assignee marker (persists derived state that the resolver already recomputes).

Mechanism: the shared 3-state resolver returns ("", True, False) for an unmappable value at
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py:110-111 ("unmappable -> desired unassigned"). That is NOT the converged sentinel, so outbound_field_diff.py:408-411 falls to the else branch and emits changed["assignee"] = "", which is what re-emits every pass. Returning the converged sentinel (None, True, False) instead makes 408 emit nothing.

Why this is lossless: the deliberate-unassign path is already separate — an empty local_value returns at identity_model.py:98-99 before the unmappable branch is reachable — so an intentional unassign still pushes. Only the unresolvable case changes.

This also satisfies the originating requirement in epic 0e68: an incoming tracker assignee is never destroyed by a local value rebar cannot resolve.

Note for whoever implements: the resolver is still CALLED each pass, so the live user-search per unmappable assignee remains even though no mutation is emitted (_assignee_cache in outbound_differ.py:381 is per-pass only). If pass duration or API volume matters at the 323-ticket scale in the reproduction, negative-result caching is a separate follow-up, not part of the convergence fix.

compiled_state.description:
## Reproduction Steps

1. Sync a rebar store to Jira (e.g. the REB cutover) where local tickets have
   assignees that are not Jira users (agent names like `claude`, `claude-opus`).
2. Run `rebar reconcile --mode dry-run` after the initial create pass.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** once a ticket is created+bound and its synced fields match, the
  reconciler emits no further mutations for it (convergence).
- **Actual:** ~323 of 355 bound tickets emit an `assignee` update every pass. The
  local assignee (e.g. `claude`) is not a Jira user, so the applier soft-fails the
  assign (`assignee 'claude' cannot be assigned — retrying without assignee`),
  Jira stays unassigned, and `_assignee_matches("claude", None)` is False — so the
  differ re-emits the same assignee update on the next pass. Perpetual churn (passes
  still succeed; the canary stays green — this is noise/inefficiency, not failure).

## Root cause

`outbound_differ._diff_fields` + `_assignee_matches`: a local assignee that cannot
be resolved to a Jira account never matches Jira's (unassigned) state, and there is
no "unresolvable assignee → don't re-emit" suppression after the applier soft-fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bound ticket whose local assignee cannot be assigned in Jira does NOT
      re-emit an assignee update every pass (converge or suppress-after-soft-fail).
- [ ] Decide the intended semantics: skip assignee sync for non-Jira-user
      assignees, map agent identities to a service account, or record an
      unresolvable-assignee marker so the differ stops re-emitting.
- [ ] A dry-run after convergence shows 0 perpetual assignee-only updates.
compiled_state.title: Reconciler churns assignee updates for non-Jira-user assignees (never converges)
